title: Dependency Record
description: The Dependency state variable: how difficult withdrawal or substitution of a system has become. Dependence converts technical risk into structural risk (Law V); as dependence increases, reversibility decreases unless deliberately replenished. The record separates nominal from operational reversibility (Law VI) and names the capacities the institution must preserve so it can still question, replace, or withdraw the system (Law XII).

schema_version.title: Schema version
schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record conforms to.

dependency_id.title: Dependency record identifier
dependency_id.description: Stable identifier for this record, referenced by grants and safety object models.

system_ref.title: System reference
system_ref.description: Identifier of the system whose dependence is being assessed.

assessed_at.title: Assessed at
assessed_at.description: When the assessment was made. Dependence is a state variable and must be re-measured.

dependents.title: Dependents
dependents.description: Workflows, roles, customers, downstream software, vendors, or infrastructure that now rely on the system.

items.title: Dependent
items.description: One party or process that depends on the system.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What kind of dependent this is.

criticality.title: Criticality
criticality.description: How badly the dependent is affected if the system is withdrawn.

substitution_cost.title: Substitution cost
substitution_cost.description: What it would cost to replace the system with an alternative.

estimate.title: Estimate
estimate.description: Numeric estimate of the substitution cost.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Unit of the estimate, for example person-weeks or currency.

expertise_retained.title: Expertise retained
expertise_retained.description: Whether the institution still holds the skills needed to do the work without the system.

last_exercised.title: Last exercised
last_exercised.description: When the retained expertise was last used in practice.

alternatives.title: Alternatives
alternatives.description: Known substitutes and whether they are still usable.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether the alternative is available, degraded, or removed.

last_exercised.title: Last exercised
last_exercised.description: When the alternative was last actually used.

last_withdrawal_rehearsal.title: Last withdrawal rehearsal
last_withdrawal_rehearsal.description: The most recent practice run of withdrawing the system. A correction that has never been rehearsed is nominal, not operational (Law VI).

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: Whether the rehearsal succeeded, partially succeeded, or failed.

correction_latency.title: Correction latency
correction_latency.description: How long it takes to detect and reverse a harmful decision produced by the system.

estimate_hours.title: Estimate (hours)
estimate_hours.description: Estimated end-to-end correction latency in hours.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: How the estimate was produced, for example measured from the latency tracker.

reversibility.title: Reversibility
reversibility.description: Three levels of reversibility, each with evidence. Technical means the change can be undone; operational means it can be undone by the people on shift within the correction window; institutional means it can be undone without unacceptable damage to the institution.

technical.title: Technical reversibility
technical.description: Can the effects be undone in the system itself?

operational.title: Operational reversibility
operational.description: Can the people and processes actually exercise the reversal in time?

institutional.title: Institutional reversibility
institutional.description: Can the institution survive exercising the reversal?

preserved_capacities.title: Preserved capacities
preserved_capacities.description: Capacities the institution deliberately keeps so it can still question, replace, or withdraw the system (Law XII).

items.title: Preserved capacity
items.description: One capacity kept in reserve and who owns keeping it.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Role accountable for keeping the capacity alive.

exposure_score.title: Exposure score
exposure_score.description: Structural exposure created by dependence. score = dependency_depth × substitution_cost × correction_latency, where dependency_depth is a unitless count of critical dependents, substitution_cost is in the unit stated in the substitution_cost object, and correction_latency is in hours. The product is a unitless index used to compare systems and trigger reconsideration when a dependency threshold is crossed.

substitution_cost.title: Substitution cost factor
substitution_cost.description: Substitution cost estimate, in the unit stated in the substitution_cost object.

feasibility.title: Feasibility
feasibility.description: Whether a level of reversibility is feasible, with the evidence for the claim.

feasible.title: Feasible
feasible.description: Whether reversal at this level is feasible.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Evidence for the feasibility claim, for example a rehearsal outcome.
